questions.title: GATE EE 2020 | GA Question: 1
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question: A circuit outputs a digit in the form of $4$ bits. $0$ is represented by $0000, 1$ by $0001, \ldots, 9$ by $1001$. A combinational circuit is to be designed which takes these $4$ bits as input and outputs $1$ if the digit $\geq$ $5$, and $0$ otherwise. If only $\textsf{AND}, \textsf{OR}$ and $\textsf{NOT}$ gates may be used, what is the minimum number of gates required?
questions.rawQuestionHtml:
A circuit outputs a digit in the form of $4$ bits. $0$ is represented by $0000, 1$ by $0001, \ldots, 9$ by $1001$. A combinational circuit is to be designed which takes these $4$ bits as input and outputs $1$ if the digit $\geq$ $5$, and $0$ otherwise. If only $\textsf{AND}, \textsf{OR}$ and $\textsf{NOT}$ gates may be used, what is the minimum number of gates required?

  1. $2$
  2. $3$
  3. $4$
  4. $5$

questions.title: GATE EE 2020 | GA Question: 6
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
The atomic fetch-and-set $x, y$ instruction unconditionally sets the memory location $x$ to $1$ and fetches the old value of $x$ in $y$ without allowing any intervening access to the memory location $x$. Consider the following implementation of $P$ and $V$ functions on a binary semaphore $S$.

void P (binary_semaphore *s) { 
    unsigned y; 
    unsigned *x = &(s->value); 
    do { 
        fetch-and-set x, y; 
    } while (y); 
}

void V (binary_semaphore *s) { 
    S->value = 0; 
}

Which one of the following is true?
questions.rawQuestionHtml:
The atomic fetch-and-set $x, y$ instruction unconditionally sets the memory location $x$ to $1$ and fetches the old value of $x$ in $y$ without allowing any intervening access to the memory location $x$. Consider the following implementation of $P$ and $V$ functions on a binary semaphore $S$.

void P (binary_semaphore *s) { 
    unsigned y; 
    unsigned *x = &(s->value); 
    do { 
        fetch-and-set x, y; 
    } while (y); 
}

void V (binary_semaphore *s) { 
    S->value = 0; 
}

Which one of the following is true? 

  1. The implementation may not work if context switching is disabled in $P$ 
  2. Instead of using fetch-and –set, a pair of normal load/store can be used 
  3. The implementation of $V$ is wrong
  4. The code does not implement a binary semaphore

questions.title: GATE EE 2020 | GA Question: 10
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question: Consider three processes, all arriving at time zero, with total execution time of $10$, $20$ and $30$ units, respectively. Each process spends the first $\text{20%}$ of execution time doing I/O, the next $\text{70%}$ of time doing computation, and the last $\text{10%}$ of time doing I/O again. The operating system uses a shortest remaining compute time first scheduling algorithm and schedules a new process either when the running process gets blocked on I/O or when the running process finishes its compute burst. Assume that all I/O operations can be overlapped as much as possible. For what percentage of time does the CPU remain idle?
questions.rawQuestionHtml:
Consider three processes, all arriving at time zero, with total execution time of $10$, $20$ and $30$ units, respectively. Each process spends the first $\text{20%}$ of execution time doing I/O, the next $\text{70%}$ of time doing computation, and the last $\text{10%}$ of time doing I/O again. The operating system uses a shortest remaining compute time first scheduling algorithm and schedules a new process either when the running process gets blocked on I/O or when the running process finishes its compute burst. Assume that all I/O operations can be overlapped as much as possible. For what percentage of time does the CPU remain idle?

  1. $\text{0%}$
  2. $\text{10.6%}$
  3. $\text{30.0%}$
  4. $\text{89.4%}$

questions.title: GATE EE 2020 | EE Question: 1
questions.subject: Electrical & Electronic Measurements
questions.question: A Permanent Magnet Moving Coil (PMMC) instrument responds strictly to:
options: The true average (DC) value of current
The Root Mean Square (RMS) value of current
The peak-to-peak amplitude
The instantaneous power

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: The true average (DC) value of current
structuredOptions.html: The true average (DC) value of current

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: The Root Mean Square (RMS) value of current
structuredOptions.html: The Root Mean Square (RMS) value of current

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: The peak-to-peak amplitude
structuredOptions.html: The peak-to-peak amplitude

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: The instantaneous power
structuredOptions.html: The instantaneous power

questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Electrical & Electronic Measurements):

Because deflecting torque in PMMC is proportional to instantaneous current ($T_d = BINA$), over an AC cycle the net torque averages out to zero. Hence it strictly registers the average (DC) component.

The Root Mean Square (RMS) value of current
The peak-to-peak amplitude
The instantaneous power

structuredOptions.html: The true average (DC) value of current

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: The Root Mean Square (RMS) value of current
structuredOptions.html: The Root Mean Square (RMS) value of current

structuredOptions.text: The peak-to-peak amplitude

Because deflecting torque in PMMC is proportional to instantaneous current ($T_d = BINA$), over an AC cycle the net torque averages out to zero. Hence it strictly registers the average (DC) component.

questions.title: GATE EE 2020 | EE Question: 26
questions.subject: Electric Circuits & Networks
questions.question: A DC voltage source $V_s = 24\text{ V}$ with internal resistance $R_s = 6\,\Omega$ is connected to a variable load resistor $R_L$. According to the maximum power transfer theorem, the maximum power (in Watts) absorbed by $R_L$ is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Electric Circuits & Networks):

Maximum power transfer occurs when $R_L = R_s = 6\,\Omega$. Maximum power $P_{\text{max}} = \frac{V_{\text{th}}^2}{4 R_{\text{th}}} = \frac{24^2}{4 \times 6} = \frac{576}{24} = 24\text{ W}$.

questions.title: GATE EE 2020 | EE Question: 27
questions.subject: Electric Circuits & Networks
questions.question: A series $RLC$ circuit has $R = 10\,\Omega$, $L = 0.1\text{ H}$, and $C = 10\,\mu\text{F}$ ($10^{-5}\text{ F}$). The resonant frequency $\omega_0$ (in $\text{rad/s}$) of the circuit is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Electric Circuits & Networks):

At resonance, $X_L = X_C \implies \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{L C}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{0.1 \times 10^{-5}}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{10^{-6}}} = \frac{1}{10^{-3}} = 1000\text{ rad/s}$.

questions.title: GATE EE 2020 | EE Question: 33
questions.subject: Electrical Machines
questions.question: A $10\text{ kVA}$, $2000/200\text{ V}$, $50\text{ Hz}$ single-phase transformer has full-load iron loss of $150\text{ W}$ and full-load copper loss of $250\text{ W}$. The maximum efficiency occurs at a fraction $x$ of full load equal to ________ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Electrical Machines):

Maximum efficiency occurs when variable copper loss equals constant iron loss: $x^2 P_{cu} = P_i \implies x = \sqrt{\frac{P_i}{P_{cu}}} = \sqrt{\frac{150}{250}} = \sqrt{0.6} \approx 0.7746 = 0.77$ of full load.

questions.title: GATE EE 2020 | EE Question: 34
questions.subject: Electrical Machines
questions.question: A 4-pole, $50\text{ Hz}$, 3-phase induction motor runs at a rotor speed of $1440\text{ rpm}$. The synchronous speed is $1500\text{ rpm}$. The percentage slip $s$ of the motor is ________ percent.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Electrical Machines):

Synchronous speed $N_s = \frac{120 f}{P} = \frac{120 \times 50}{4} = 1500\text{ rpm}$. Slip $s = \frac{N_s - N}{N_s} \times 100\% = \frac{1500 - 1440}{1500} \times 100\% = \frac{60}{1500} \times 100\% = 4.0\%$.

questions.question: A $400\text{ kV}$, 3-phase lossless transmission line has total series inductance $L = 1.0\text{ mH/km}$ and shunt capacitance $C = 0.01\,\mu\text{F/km}$. The surge impedance $Z_c = \sqrt{L/C}$ (in Ohms) of the line is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Power Systems & Protection):

$Z_c = \sqrt{\frac{L}{C}} = \sqrt{\frac{1.0 \times 10^{-3}}{0.01 \times 10^{-6}}} = \sqrt{10^5} = 316.23\,\Omega$.

questions.title: GATE EE 2020 | EE Question: 51
questions.subject: Control Systems
questions.question: The open-loop transfer function of a unity feedback system is $G(s) = \frac{K}{s(s+2)(s+4)}$. Using Routh-Hurwitz stability criterion, the maximum value of $K$ for closed-loop stability is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Control Systems):

Characteristic equation: $1 + G(s) = 0 \implies s(s^2 + 6s + 8) + K = 0 \implies s^3 + 6s^2 + 8s + K = 0$. Routh array first column entries: $s^3: 1$, $s^2: 6$, $s^1: \frac{6(8) - K}{6} = \frac{48 - K}{6}$, $s^0: K$. For stability, all terms must be positive: $48 - K > 0 \implies K < 48$.
